precepts.text: Learn not the way of the heathen, and be not dismayed at the signs of heaven; the decked tree is the custom of the people and is vain, and the stargazing, the probes, and the planet colonies are the signs of heaven the heathen are dismayed at.
precepts.point: The main abomination we bring into our house is the Christmas tree of Jeremiah 10: the tree cut down, fastened with nails and hammers, and decked with silver and with gold, whether cut from the forest or bought as a fake tree from the store.

note.label: Deuteronomy 7: A Holy People, Chosen Above All People

precepts.why:
“Hear ye the word which the Lord speaketh unto you, O house of Israel: Thus saith the Lord, Learn not the way of the heathen, and be not dismayed at the signs of heaven; for the heathen are dismayed at them.” The stargazing, the probes and the planet colonies are the signs of heaven the heathen are dismayed at.

“For the customs of the people are vain: for one cutteth a tree out of the forest, the work of the hands of the workman, with the axe. They deck it with silver and with gold; they fasten it with nails and with hammers, that it move not.” That is the Christmas tree, the main abomination we bring into our house, whether cut from the forest or bought as a fake tree from the store. The decked tree is the custom of the people, and it is vain: “They are upright as the palm tree, but speak not: they must needs be borne, because they cannot go.”

Moses said “Neither shalt thou bring an abomination into thine house, lest thou be a cursed thing like it”, and not to desire the silver or gold that is on their gods. Bring it up to today: the Jesus pieces, the crosses, the ankhs and the rosary beads wrapped around the neck and rubbed in prayer make the wearer an abomination and a cursed thing just like the idol, and so does the tree decked with silver and with gold. “Be not afraid of them; for they cannot do evil, neither also is it in them to do good.”

precepts.text: When he uttereth his voice there is a multitude of waters in the heavens; he maketh lightnings with rain and bringeth forth the wind out of his treasures.
precepts.point: The Most High sent out arrows and lightning and scattered his enemies, and the channels of the sea and the foundations of the world were discovered at the rebuking of the Lord, at the blast of the breath of his nostrils. His power over creation is total.

note.label: 2 Samuel 22: The Lord Is My Rock and My Fortress

precepts.why:
“He hath made the earth by his power, he hath established the world by his wisdom, and hath stretched out the heavens by his discretion. When he uttereth his voice, there is a multitude of waters in the heavens”, and “he maketh lightnings with rain, and bringeth forth the wind out of his treasures.”

David sang, “The Lord thundered from heaven, and the most High uttered his voice. And he sent out arrows, and scattered them; lightning, and discomfited them.” What we hear as thunder is the Most High speaking. Esau says the thunder is only clouds clashing; the scripture says it is the voice of the Lord, and after his voice there is a multitude of waters, meaning the rain that follows.

The one who made the earth by his power rules all of it: “the channels of the sea appeared, the foundations of the world were discovered, at the rebuking of the Lord, at the blast of the breath of his nostrils.” His power over creation is total.

precepts.text: The way of a man is not in himself; it is not in man that walks to direct his own steps, confirming that Job's trials and our walk are under the hand of the Most High.
precepts.point: Job knows he is not in the sin these brothers claim; he contests everything they say. He understands the whole purpose of his situation is Satan trying to prove that a man put through certain things will curse God, and that was not Job's case. What he is going through can be applied to our captivity in this country today.

note.label: Job 16: Miserable Comforters Are Ye All

precepts.why:
“O Lord, I know that the way of man is not in himself: it is not in man that walketh to direct his steps.” It is not in man to direct his own steps. This confirms that Job's trials and our walk are under the hand of the Most High.

Job knows he is not in the sin these brothers claim and contests everything they say; his witness is in heaven and his record is on high. He understands the whole purpose of his situation is Satan trying to prove that a man put through certain things will curse God, and that was not Job's case. His steps were being directed. “When a few years are come, then I shall go the way whence I shall not return.” What he is going through can be applied to our captivity in this country today: the way is not in us, it is under his hand.

precepts.text: A man's way is not in himself; his steps are directed by the Most High.
precepts.point: Man's goings are of the Most High. A lot of us were guided into the truth and do not understand it. You did not come in just because a friend shared a flyer or you found a random YouTube video. It was not random.

note.label: Proverbs 21: The Most High Rules the Heart of the King

precepts.why:
“The king’s heart is in the hand of the Lord, as the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will.” The mind of the king is controlled by the Most High. Just as Pharaoh's heart was hardened against Moses and Israel, the Most High can harden the hearts of kings and soften them, and he used heathen kings to deal in our favor, like Cyrus in the time of Ezra, who did things in favor of our people.

Jeremiah says it is not only kings: “O Lord, I know that the way of man is not in himself: it is not in man that walketh to direct his steps.” A man's way is not in himself; his steps are directed by the Most High. Man's goings are of the Most High.

A lot of us were guided into the truth and do not understand it. You did not come in just because a friend shared a flyer or you found a random YouTube video. It was not random. The same hand that turns the king's heart directed your steps here.

Every way of a man is right in his own eyes, but the Most High weighs the heart, and he is the one directing the steps.
